title: Kid Thomas photo and the musician who plays two horns at once
summary: Barker never worked with Kid Thomas; the photo shows his studio, his pupil and pictures of him playing two instruments at once, which Friedlander recalls hearing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: Look at that painting in the background. That's Larry Barnstein. That's Kid Thomas. I didn't know Kid Thomas personally. You didn't know him?
Looks good. Well, when we used to go down there, that's a gig. It's manual.
You dig the meaning of that picture, huh? Uh-huh. The meaning there.
You know where the... You know where the... You know where the...
You know where the... You know where the... You know where the... You know where the...
Ashtray. With a difference, huh? Yeah.
His ashtray? He has his pupil sitting on the other side of that music stand. See, notice... What... Pay Before Serve. And there in the background is pictures of him playing two instruments at once.
You can't see it too clear, but I've been in that studio many a time.
But did you ever hear him play? Did you ever tape that? I think they might have taped it at the stage.
Well I have some here. He came in the house one day and he played the two horns for him. Oh yeah.
And it's a wonderful jazz man to hear the way he does the two horns, you know? Sure is.
He used to play Chris Kelly's Love in harmony, and then play the variations and everything. That's old slow driving. Yes. You know who that is? No I don't. And Cook. You still living?
